review_evidence: Codex self-review: source-map alignment, original prose, Class 4 pedagogy, answer keys, and own-words grading
Focused checks: canonical hash, key-option consistency, stage and assessment freshness, skill coverage, and chapter/corpus quality
title: Together We Can
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Find how a team succeeds
levels.focus: identify a paragraph main idea and support it with evidence
levels.teaching_goal: State what a teamwork paragraph is mainly about and point to actions that support that idea.

guided_check.teaching_block: A main idea covers the whole paragraph. Here every action repairs the same play area, so the main idea is the class working together to improve it.
guided_check.passage: The play corner was untidy after art club. Rhea stacked the games, Zubin sorted the crayons, and Farah wiped the tables. Before the bell, the corner was ready for the next class.
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence best states the paragraph's main idea?
options: The children worked together to prepare the play corner.
accepted_answers: The children worked together to prepare the play corner.

bridge.teaching_block: Break the paragraph into three parts: shared problem, different actions, shared result. Then combine those parts into one idea.
bridge.passage: A windstorm scattered paper across the courtyard. One group collected sheets, another held open sacks, and a third checked the drains. The courtyard was clear by assembly.
bridge.prompt: What shared result did the groups produce?

masterclass.teaching_block: A common mistake is choosing one memorable detail as the main idea. The main idea must explain why all the listed jobs belong in the paragraph.
masterclass.passage: For the class exhibition, Arun tested the lamp, Diya fixed the labels, and Hamid placed models on the table. Their different jobs made the science stall ready.
masterclass.prompt: Which answer is broad enough to include every detail?
options: Different contributions prepared one science stall.
The labels were made of paper.
accepted_answers: Different contributions prepared one science stall.

independent_check.teaching_block: Read the new paragraph and decide what all its details show.
independent_check.passage: The lane library had received two boxes of books. Mehak recorded the titles, Joel stamped each cover, and Bina arranged the books by topic. Visitors could borrow them that evening.
independent_check.prompt: State the main idea and mention one detail that supports it.

concept_slots.description: states that the group prepared or organised the library books
mentions one supporting action from the paragraph

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same main-idea-and-evidence method in a community setting.
transfer_check.passage: After heavy rain, residents wanted the bus stop usable again. Mr Sen swept mud, two teenagers moved fallen branches, and Lata placed a warning sign beside a puddle. Commuters soon had a clear place to wait.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain the paragraph's main idea in your own words and support it with one action.

concept_slots.description: states that residents worked together to make the bus stop usable or safe
uses one action as evidence

levels.title: Read teamwork words in context
levels.focus: infer the meaning of cooperation words from nearby clues
levels.teaching_goal: Use actions and results around an unfamiliar word to explain its meaning.

guided_check.teaching_block: Context clues can show a word's meaning. When people plan together, divide jobs, and finish one goal, the clues show that cooperate means work together.
guided_check.passage: The young gardeners cooperated: one dug holes, one placed seeds, and one carried water.

bridge.teaching_block: Look for the result caused by the unfamiliar word. If combined efforts make a heavy object move, combined means joined together.
bridge.passage: Their combined effort moved the cupboard: Neel pushed while Sara guided it.

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not guess from a word's sound. Test each meaning against the whole sentence. A contribution is something a person gives or does to help a shared task.
masterclass.passage: Everyone made a contribution to the mural. Pema sketched birds, Laksh mixed paint, and Ira cleaned the brushes.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the consequence in this fresh sentence to infer the central word.
independent_check.passage: The relay team showed unity. Even after one runner stumbled, the others encouraged her and finished together.
independent_check.prompt: What does unity mean in this sentence?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Carry context reading into a music setting.
transfer_check.passage: The musicians were in harmony: the drum kept a steady beat while the flute and voices fitted smoothly around it.
transfer_check.prompt: What does in harmony suggest about how the musicians performed?

concept_slots.description: explains that the musicians worked or sounded well together
refers to a clue from the sentence

levels.title: Choose precise group nouns
levels.focus: use collective nouns as naming words in meaningful sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Identify a collective noun by the group it names and use agreement clues in context.

guided_check.teaching_block: A collective noun is one naming word for a group. Team names a group of players, so it is the collective noun in the sentence.
guided_check.passage: The team practises passing the ball every morning.
guided_check.prompt: In this sentence, which word gathers the players into one group?

bridge.teaching_block: First identify what is grouped, then choose the matching group word. A choir is a group of singers.
bridge.passage: A choir of twelve singers performs at the school fair.

masterclass.teaching_block: A common mistake is treating every plural noun as a collective noun. Children names more than one child; class is the single word naming them as one group.
masterclass.passage: The class carries its notebooks to the hall.
masterclass.prompt: Which word is the collective noun?

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the sentence meaning to supply the precise group word.
independent_check.passage: A _____ of dancers moved onto the stage together.
independent_check.prompt: Complete the sentence with a suitable collective noun.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use a group noun in a nature context rather than a school context.
transfer_check.passage: At dusk, a _____ of birds crossed the orange sky.
transfer_check.prompt: Write a collective noun that fits the sentence.

levels.title: Join an action to its reason
levels.focus: use because, but, and so to connect teamwork evidence and reasons
levels.teaching_goal: Select a connector that shows cause, contrast, or result and write an evidence-backed reason.

guided_check.teaching_block: Because introduces a cause. The second idea explains why Tara held the chart steady.
guided_check.passage: Tara held the chart steady because Vikram was pinning the corners.
guided_check.prompt: Which connector signals why Tara holds the chart steady?

bridge.teaching_block: Ask how the ideas are related. Use but for contrast and so for a result.
bridge.passage: The first plan failed, _____ the group tried a simpler design.
bridge.prompt: Which connector fits the unexpected change in the group's plan?

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not use because when the second part is a result. In 'The rope was short, so they joined another rope,' joining is the result of the problem.
masterclass.passage: The boxes were heavy, _____ four neighbours carried them together.
masterclass.prompt: Which connector correctly shows the result?

independent_check.teaching_block: Connect the action and the evidence without a sentence frame.
independent_check.passage: The poster stayed straight. Ayaan measured the top edge while Mira held the ruler.
independent_check.prompt: Explain why the poster stayed straight.

concept_slots.description: states that the poster stayed straight or was aligned
mentions measuring or holding the ruler as the cause

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use a connector to explain a cause in a kitchen task.
transfer_check.passage: The fruit salad was ready quickly. One cousin washed the fruit while another chopped it and a third set out bowls.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one sentence explaining why the salad was ready quickly.

concept_slots.description: uses a cause or result connector
mentions two or more people dividing the work

levels.title: Write a fair team solution
levels.focus: summarise a group problem and propose a fair solution in own words
levels.teaching_goal: Write complete sentences that name a disagreement, propose a fair action, and explain how it helps the group.

guided_check.teaching_block: A fair solution recognises both needs. Worked example: 'The groups can take turns using the court, so each gets practice time.' It gives an action and a fair result.
guided_check.passage: The red team and blue team both want the only skipping rope during break.
options: The teams can take equal turns with the rope.
The red team should hide the rope.
No one should ever use the rope.
The louder team should keep it.
accepted_answers: The teams can take equal turns with the rope.

bridge.teaching_block: Build the solution in three steps: name both sides, choose a share-or-turn action, then state the benefit.
bridge.passage: Two project groups need the same tablet to record their presentations.
bridge.prompt: Which first step leads to a fair plan?
options: ask how long each group needs the tablet
give it to the tallest child
accepted_answers: ask how long each group needs the tablet

masterclass.teaching_block: Fair does not always mean doing exactly the same thing. It means each person gets what is reasonably needed. A child with a larger map may need a little more table space.
masterclass.passage: A small model and a large map must share one display table.
masterclass.prompt: Which plan responds to the actual needs?
options: Give the map more space and keep a clear area for the model.
Cut the map until both objects are the same size.
Put both objects on top of each other.
accepted_answers: Give the map more space and keep a clear area for the model.

independent_check.teaching_block: Write the solution yourself; do not copy a model sentence.
independent_check.passage: Four children must present, but there are only two speaking parts in the current plan.
independent_check.prompt: Write two complete sentences: summarise the problem and propose a fair solution.

concept_slots.description: states that four children need roles but only two speaking parts exist
proposes adding, sharing, rotating, or dividing roles
uses enough words to express the problem and solution

transfer_check.passage: Three families in a building want to water the shared terrace plants, but watering them three times would waste water.
transfer_check.prompt: In your own words, describe the problem and suggest a fair plan.

concept_slots.description: notes that repeated watering would waste water
suggests a schedule, rotation, or shared responsibility
explains that plants are cared for without wasting water

items.passage: A class wanted a weather board. Kian drew symbols, Rupa checked temperatures, and Ben wrote the dates. The board was finished before lunch.
items.prompt: Which statement captures the weather-board paragraph as a whole?
options: Children used different jobs to complete a weather board.
Only Ben worked on the board.
accepted_answers: Children used different jobs to complete a weather board.

items.passage: At the book sale, Ina arranged prices, Mohit packed purchases, and Saira answered visitors' questions.
items.prompt: State the main idea and one detail that supports it.

concept_slots.description: states that people worked together to run the book sale
mentions one action as evidence

items.passage: The footpath was blocked by dry twigs. Dev gathered them, his sister held the basket, and their neighbour swept the dust.
items.prompt: Which detail best supports the idea that the neighbours cooperated?
options: Each person completed a different part of clearing the path.
accepted_answers: Each person completed a different part of clearing the path.

items.passage: A puppet show needed a curtain, voices, and music. Three friends each prepared one of those parts.
items.prompt: Explain why the show could go ahead.

concept_slots.description: explains that friends completed the needed parts
connects their work to the show being ready

items.passage: The hikers coordinated their steps: the front walker called out stones while the others followed the same safe path.
items.prompt: What does coordinated mean?

items.passage: The committee reached a consensus after every member agreed to hold the fair on Friday.
items.prompt: Use the context to explain consensus.

items.passage: Roshni's contribution was designing the invitation while others planned the games.
items.prompt: Which action was Roshni's contribution?

items.passage: The rowers moved in unison; every paddle entered the water at the same moment.
items.prompt: What clue shows the meaning of in unison?
accepted_answers: every paddle entered at the same moment

items.passage: A band of musicians waited beside the stage.
items.prompt: Identify the collective noun in the sentence.

items.passage: A _____ of bees circled the flowering tree.
items.prompt: Supply the precise collective noun.

items.passage: The fleet sailed out of the harbour at dawn.
items.prompt: What does fleet name?

items.passage: A _____ of actors bowed after the play.
items.prompt: Write a suitable collective noun.

items.passage: The glue had dried, _____ the group opened a fresh bottle.
items.prompt: Which connector links the dry glue to the group's next action?

items.passage: The lanterns hung evenly. Gita marked equal spaces before Omar tied them.
items.prompt: Explain why the lanterns hung evenly.

concept_slots.description: mentions that the lanterns were equally spaced
uses Gita's marking as the reason

items.passage: The room was small, _____ everyone found a useful job.
items.prompt: Choose the connector that shows contrast.

items.passage: The seed packets were sorted quickly because two children read labels while another filled the trays.
items.prompt: Give the evidence-backed reason for the quick sorting.

concept_slots.description: mentions the divided sorting actions
links those actions to quick sorting

items.passage: Two clubs need the hall at the same time for rehearsals.
items.prompt: Which plan is fair?
options: Make a timetable that gives each club rehearsal time.
Let one club lock the hall.
Give the hall to the club with more members.
accepted_answers: Make a timetable that gives each club rehearsal time.

items.passage: Five students want to paint, but the group has only two wide brushes.
items.prompt: Summarise the problem and propose a fair response.

concept_slots.description: states that five students share only two brushes
proposes turns, sharing, or other jobs
expresses both parts in complete ideas

items.passage: A community kitchen has one oven and three trays waiting to bake.
items.prompt: What should the cooks do first to share the oven fairly?
options: agree on an order for the trays
accepted_answers: agree on an order for the trays

items.passage: Two neighbours disagree about whether a shared wall should be blue or green.
items.prompt: In your own words, describe a solution that listens to both neighbours.

concept_slots.description: recognises both colour choices or neighbours
offers a compromise or decision method
shows discussion or fairness
